title: Rings of Power Season 3 Trailer Unveils Simon Pegg as the Balrog
excerpt: Prime Video debuted the first footage from its fantasy epic's third season at San Diego Comic-Con, alongside a wave of new castings headlined by Pegg voicing the iconic creature for the first time in any Tolkien adaptation.
body:
Amazon's The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power pulled back the curtain on its third season at San Diego Comic-Con on Friday, dropping a one-minute teaser trailer and announcing several major casting additions during its Hall H panel. The headline surprise: Simon Pegg will voice the Balrog, marking the first time the fiery demon of shadow and flame has spoken in any screen adaptation of J.R.R. Tolkien's mythology.

  • Simon Pegg will voice the Balrog in Season 3, making it the first time the iconic creature speaks in any Tolkien adaptation.
  • The first teaser trailer debuted at Comic-Con's Hall H panel, teasing Sauron's obsessive quest to forge the One Ring — described by showrunners as "unhinged."
  • New cast additions include Jamie Campbell Bower as Celeborn, Eddie Marsan as Thrain, and Andrew Richardson as Anarion, alongside the debut of the Nazgnagôl.
  • The eight-episode season premieres November 11, 2026 on Prime Video, with the first four episodes dropping on launch day.

A Talking Balrog and a Stacked New Cast

https://youtube.com/watch?v=x8UAUAuKNcU

The Pegg casting drew an immediate reaction from the Hall H crowd. The Balrog, which first appeared in Season 2 and killed King Durin III in the finale, has until now been a wordless force of destruction across Tolkien screen adaptations — from Peter Jackson's The Fellowship of the Ring onward. Giving the creature a voice represents a significant creative departure for the series.

https://x.com/DiscussingFilm/status/2080719187551326567

Pegg, known for Shaun of the Dead, the Mission: Impossible franchise, and Star Trek, takes on one of his darkest roles. Prime Video did not include his vocal performance in the teaser, keeping his interpretation under wraps for now. According to ScreenRant, Sauron will face off against the Balrog in Season 3 and "must learn from" the ancient being — suggesting the creature plays a far larger narrative role than in previous seasons.

Beyond Pegg, the panel revealed several new additions. Jamie Campbell Bower, best known as Vecna in Netflix's Stranger Things, will play Celeborn, Galadriel's long-lost husband — a character teased since the show's first season. His casting was confirmed earlier in the week through Empire magazine, where Bower described Celeborn as a "lover-boy" driven by "longing and yearning."

"This idea of longing and yearning is so pervasive."

— Jamie Campbell Bower, on his character Celeborn, to Empire

Other new cast members include Eddie Marsan (Clayface) as Thrain, King Durin IV's older brother; Andrew Richardson as Anarion, Elendil's younger son and Isildur's brother; Zubin Varla (Andor) as Khamûl the Easterling of Rhûn; and Adam Young (Masters of the Air) as Marnûkh, described as "a mysterious Orc who may not be what he seems."

The One Ring and the Rise of the Nazgnagôl

The teaser trailer opens with Charlie Vickers' Sauron declaring, "Now is the mighty hour come," before cutting through rapid shots of war, the forging process of the One Ring, and the growing alliance of Middle-earth's remaining free peoples. Showrunners J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay told the audience that Season 3 is deeply rooted in Sauron's psychology, with the Dark Lord spending the five-year time jump obsessively — and unsuccessfully — attempting to forge his master weapon.

Payne and McKay described the eventual forging sequence as "unhinged," a word that caught fans off guard. The trailer shows early stages of the process but holds back the full reveal.

The panel also introduced the Nazgnagôl, Sauron's Second Age ring-servants and the predecessors to the Third Age's Nazgûl — the Ringwraiths familiar to Lord of the Rings fans. Four armored Nazgnagôl made a surprise in-person appearance at the panel, interrupting the proceedings to dramatic effect. According to the showrunners, the Nazgnagôl are hunting the three Elven rings so Sauron can reverse-engineer them to create the One Ring.

Five Years Later: Where Season 3 Picks Up

Season 3 is set five years after the fall of Eregion, which served as Season 2's climactic event. Sauron's armies have swept across Middle-earth, leaving only a few isolated strongholds: Khazad-dûm, where the Dwarves are sealed within their mountain halls, and the elven realms of Lindon and Rivendell, protected by the Three Rings.

Gandalf (Daniel Weyman), confirmed as The Stranger at the end of Season 2, has spent the intervening years training with Tom Bombadil. Tar-Míriel (Cynthia Addai-Robinson) is now in exile following a coup in Númenor and is rallying a resistance movement. The showrunners teased that Númenor's storyline looms large this season.

"It feels like the Cold War... it's an intense season."

— J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay, showrunners

The dwarf lords, meanwhile, are searching for the rings that Prince Durin IV (Owain Arthur) has hidden, and his children are now teenagers — a detail that shifts the family's dynamic heading into the new season.

What's Next for the Series

Season 3 will premiere on November 11, 2026 with its first four episodes, followed by two batches of two episodes in the subsequent weeks, totaling eight — matching the format of previous seasons. A special in-room-only featurette at Comic-Con titled "Bringing Season 3's Creatures to Life" previewed Pegg's Balrog, Fell-beasts, the war elephants known as Mûmakil, and the show's upgraded Orcs.

Reports from May indicated that Amazon has begun early development on Season 4, though no official announcement has been made. Given the scale of the production — still the most expensive television series ever made — the early start is consistent with the logistical demands of bringing Tolkien's Second Age to screen.

The Hall H panel was moderated by Benjamin Walker, who plays High King Gil-galad, and featured Payne, McKay, Addai-Robinson, Arthur, Ismael Cruz Córdova, Vickers, Weyman, and Bower.
nri_angle: The Rings of Power is one of the most-watched fantasy series among Indian audiences on Prime Video, and the Comic-Con reveals including new Indian-origin actor Zubin Varla's casting will resonate with the show's substantial South Asian fanbase.
author: Diaspora Desk
